subject.title: fix(azure): responses model aliases route correctly

question: Should manifest aliases use the PR's context-sensitive owner/transport precedence—retaining the requested configured provider when it has an endpoint or model surface while preserving unconditional owner suppressions—or should alias ownership remain unconditional?
rationale: Both behaviors are plausible plugin-manifest contracts, and the choice affects external plugin aliases, credentials, provider routing, and upgrade compatibility; tests can prove an implementation but cannot choose the permanent API semantics.

options.title: Approve contextual alias metadata
options.body: Keep the generic helper, require an agents/OpenAI owner review, refresh onto current main, and retain the cross-provider compatibility tests before merge.

options.title: Move precedence into a generic catalog seam
options.body: Preserve the behavior but relocate the decision from the embedded-agent resolver into the shared model-catalog owner so all alias consumers use one contract.

options.title: Retain unconditional alias ownership
options.body: Do not merge this approach and design a provider-owned Azure repair that does not change shared manifest-alias semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve contextual alias metadata
recommendation.body: Keep the generic helper, require an agents/OpenAI owner review, refresh onto current main, and retain the cross-provider compatibility tests before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged provider/model routing history and embedded-agent resolver ownership make steipete the strongest available decision-routing candidate.
